questions.stem: A study group observes cos θ<0 and sin θ<0; which quadrant is θ in?

answer.exemplar: Cosine and sine both negative occur in quadrant III, where x<0 and y<0, so θ is in quadrant III.

questions.explanation: QIII has both coordinates negative, so both cos and sin negative. QII has cos<0, sin>0; QIV has cos>0, sin<0.
questions.hint: Match both negative signs to quadrant III.

questions.learningObjective: Solve log equation with domain check
questions.stem: Solve log_2(x+3)=4; first exponentiate, then solve and check domain.

options.text: x=13 because 2^4=x+3 → x=16-3=13, valid since x+3>0

questions.explanation: 2^4=x+3 → 16=x+3 → x=13. Domain x+3>0 satisfied. Option B forgets -3.

questions.topic: Log of a product, quotient, and power
questions.stem: A student simplifies log(x^3/y) as 3 log x / log y, dividing the logs.

options.text: 3 log x / log y is correct
3 log x - log y is correct

questions.explanation: log(x^3/y)=log(x^3)-log y=3 log x-log y. Dividing logs is invalid.
